races.name: Pentraeth Subaru Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: My Noble Lord
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip on Good and brings strong yard form (T14: 1/3); the confirmed front-runner who is likely to get a clean lead in this small field, though the [STYLE_FIT] flag tempers confidence if the race develops differently than expected — tongue-tie noted.

runners_data.name: Presentandcounting
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up performer with an outstanding Good-ground profile (14/15 sim-going runs placed or winning) and consistent form at this sort of trip; Theo Gillard takes over for McCain and the 51-day break is the main query, but the style suits this race shape perfectly.

runners_data.name: Country Park
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type for the O'Neill team whose best form on Good ground (9/14 sim-going) fits the likely race shape; Jonjo Jr takes the ride and the cheekpieces flag a horse that needs stoking, with the last four runs all coming at 20f or beyond suggesting the trip is fine.

runners_data.name: Le Gentleman
runners_data.note: Sharp recent winning form (1 from last 4, Good going) for the in-form Greenall/Guerriero yard, and Jack Tudor is a significant booking; naturally a prominent racer, he is likely to find himself racing further back than ideal given My Noble Lord's presence, which places a tactical question mark over how effectively he can reproduce that front-running form.

runners_data.name: Lermoos Legend
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — if declared, this 11-year-old has a solid Good-ground record (7/15 sim-going) and two wins at this sort of trip; a natural prominent type who would press My Noble Lord and is the most plausible pace companion if he does take his place.

races.paceDynamic: My Noble Lord is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Lermoos Legend and Le Gentleman both natural prominent types, there is more pace-seeking energy in this five-runner field than positions allow — My Noble Lord is likeliest to secure the lead, with Lermoos Legend and Le Gentleman likely to be shuffled back slightly from their natural roles. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all get their position; My Noble Lord holds the clearest claim to the front, Lermoos Legend the next best, while Le Gentleman is the most likely to be displaced into an unnatural midfield berth. On Good ground over 2m4½f at Bangor, a single controlled leader sets a measured, sustainable gallop — no pressure from rivals keen to dominate, no scrambling for position. This shape classically favours hold-up horses with the ability to close from off the pace in the straight, meaning Presentandcounting and Country Park, both genuine hold-up types with strong Good-ground form, are structurally best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Lead, Late Closers
scenarios.trigger: If My Noble Lord dictates an uncontested, controlled pace and hold-up runners have energy to pick off the leaders from two out.
scenarios.body: If My Noble Lord dictates an uncontested, controlled pace and hold-up runners have energy to pick off the leaders from two out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough that My Noble Lord steals an unassailable advantage and the hold-up horses cannot close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: If the pace is slow enough that My Noble Lord steals an unassailable advantage and the hold-up horses cannot close the gap in time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Lermoos Legend presses My Noble Lord into a genuinely competitive duel and the hold-up horses are left with too much to do.
scenarios.body: If Lermoos Legend presses My Noble Lord into a genuinely competitive duel and the hold-up horses are left with too much to do.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swamps Field
scenarios.trigger: If an unusually strong gallop is set and the hold-up horses produce a devastating late surge to swamp the entire field in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: If an unusually strong gallop is set and the hold-up horses produce a devastating late surge to swamp the entire field in the closing stages.

watchPoints.text: My Noble Lord sets the tempo entirely alone — if his early sectionals are slow, watch for Country Park and Presentandcounting being caught too far back to launch a meaningful challenge.

Le Gentleman's redistribution to midfield means Jack Tudor will need to make a decision early about whether to chase My Noble Lord or accept an unnatural hold-up role — an awkward tactical compromise for a horse that wins from the front.
Presentandcounting has not run for 51 days; fitness over a testing 2m4½f chase trip on Good ground is the key fitness watch-point for this hold-up type who needs to be at peak sharpness to close.

Lermoos Legend is listed as a non-runner — if a late declaration is confirmed, the entire pace dynamic shifts as a second prominent type enters to press My Noble Lord, increasing the chance of a contested gallop (Scenario C).

races.name: Wrexham Evening Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Slaney Opera
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner here; style-fit flag notes it is racing at the outer edge of its comfort zone in terms of dominance, but on Good ground with 32 days since last run, eight career wins from prominent positions give it a strong claims-based profile — the key question is whether the pace it sets is too soft to protect it late.

runners_data.name: Dazzlelikethis
runners_data.note: Lightly exposed on Good ground with just one placing from six tries on that surface, this five-year-old returns off a lengthy 224-day break (cheekpieces applied) and while the hold-up style is natural, seasonal fitness makes it hard to trust at this trip first time back.

runners_data.name: Glenmalure Flyer
runners_data.note: Six years old and returning from 570 days off under Harry Skelton for Henry De Bromhead, this horse's finishing tendency to fade is a concern over 3m, and despite a recent chase win (form peak: 1), the layoff and the flag warning about late stamina are significant negatives.

runners_data.name: Vinnie O'Neil
runners_data.note: A consistent hold-up horse whose recent form string reads 4897-6 — bluntly, nothing to recommend it in terms of winning, and on Good ground (four from seven placings in sim-going but no wins) the trip looks fine but the level appears short of what is needed.

runners_data.name: Friends Don't Ask
runners_data.note: Consistent performer in Good conditions with 13 places from 15 runs on comparable ground and four recent places; at 11 years old and genuinely a hold-up type pushed forward on the pace map, its best chance comes if it gets a clear run from the chasing pack rather than being hampered in traffic — STYLE_FIT flag tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Est Illic
runners_data.note: A 12-year-old whose true running style sits at the back of the field — mapped to midfield only because the rear is congested — and while the form shows three places in similar going, age and redistribution away from its comfort zone mean this is a prayer rather than a plan without a gap appearing.

runners_data.name: Henry Box Brown
runners_data.note: Had a fall (U) last time out which demands scrutiny at the fences; naturally a hold-up horse running in a position it won't naturally find, and with 24 days since that mishap, confidence at the obstacles is the primary concern here rather than pace suitability.

runners_data.name: Radharc Na Slaine
runners_data.note: The only other prominent-to-pace style in the race beyond Slaney Opera, with an outstanding Good-ground record (13 from 15 sim-going, one win, five places) and a recent course-distance profile that fits this race well — well-placed to track the leader and make a natural move from the second-last.

runners_data.name: Rockvale
runners_data.note: Has shown ability to finish second on Good ground (2/21f/GOO in recent form) and is a natural hold-up type placed into midfield by redistribution; at seven years old it is young enough to handle traffic, but with only 15 days since last run and a pulled-up last outing to explain, durability over 3m needs proving.

runners_data.name: Shuile Warrior
runners_data.note: On soft ground this horse has little to recommend it at the best of times (1 from 5 in sim-going), and while today's Good surface is better, a 69-day absence, a pulled-up last run, and a style that is naturally held-up but redistributed into midfield all combine to make this one of the harder profiles to recommend in this shape.

races.paceDynamic: Slaney Opera is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 3m trip on Good ground at Bangor. Radharc Na Slaine is the only other prominent-style runner and may push forward to track closely, but neither horse is likely to inject significant early pressure, meaning the pace will be steady and the field will bunch behind them through the early stages. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Friends Don't Ask, Est Illic, Henry Box Brown, Rockvale, and Shuile Warrior are all genuine come-from-behind horses who will be squeezed into a congested midfield pack rather than finding their natural deep position. With a lone front-runner setting a measured tempo over a staying trip on a fair surface, this race shape strongly favours patient, well-positioned horses who can travel into the race from the prominent-to-midfield group and sustain their effort up the straight — runners able to get a clear run from second or third will be advantaged over those stuck in traffic further back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slaney Opera Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Slaney Opera is allowed to coast in front at a controlled pace with Radharc Na Slaine tracking and no horse making a sustained bid to close until the final turn.
scenarios.body: If Slaney Opera is allowed to coast in front at a controlled pace with Radharc Na Slaine tracking and no horse making a sustained bid to close until the final turn.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady enough that a horse sitting second or third off the leader travels through the race on the bridle and produces a decisive late challenge.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely steady enough that a horse sitting second or third off the leader travels through the race on the bridle and produces a decisive late challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finds Late Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that the rear group gets a tow into the race and a clear run materialises for a finisher in the home straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that the rear group gets a tow into the race and a clear run materialises for a finisher in the home straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Slaney Opera sets a pace that proves too fast for the conditions or falls at a fence, causing the race to open up for a horse that has been travelling kindly in the pack.
scenarios.body: If Slaney Opera sets a pace that proves too fast for the conditions or falls at a fence, causing the race to open up for a horse that has been travelling kindly in the pack.

watchPoints.text: Watch Slaney Opera's jumping under Kielan Woods — if it makes a significant error early, the race opens up dramatically given there is no other confirmed front-runner to take over.

Radharc Na Slaine (Conor Ring) is the horse most likely to challenge Slaney Opera for the lead or sit a close second; if it tracks smoothly through the early stages on Good ground, its 13/15 sim-going record makes it a significant threat in the straight.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Friends Don't Ask, Est Illic, Henry Box Brown, Rockvale, Shuile Warrior) will create traffic congestion in the midfield — watch for horses finding themselves trapped on the rail at the top of the home straight with nowhere to go.

Henry Box Brown (Ellis Collier, 5lb claimer) unseated last time out — monitor its jumping at the early fences; a horse returning from a fall with a less experienced pilot at a jumping track is a risk factor for the whole field behind it.

Glenmalure Flyer returns from 570 days off under Harry Skelton — even for a top jump jockey, a horse absent that long over 3m Good ground with a known finishing fade is a significant stamina query from the top of the straight onwards.

races.name: Wrexham Lager Mares' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
Bangor-On-Dee Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Supreme Yeats
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins over 2m6f on Good ground at the same track give this Dan Skelton veteran a standout course-and-going profile, and Harry Skelton's ride from the front should allow him to set a measured tempo that showcases his jumping — the STYLE_FIT flag is less of a concern here as he is genuinely the pace-setter rather than being forced out of role.

runners_data.name: Il Va De Soi
runners_data.note: Two recent wins on Good ground over 21f suggest the trip and conditions are squarely in his favour, but Theo Gillard needs something to chase — with only four runners and one front-runner, the tempo may not be fierce enough to set up the late run that suits this genuine hold-up horse.

runners_data.name: Crystal Glance
runners_data.note: In excellent form with four wins from five Good-ground starts including a recent victory at 20f, and Jack Tudor's partnership with the Oliver Greenall & Josh Guerriero yard gives this six-year-old strong claims as the most natural danger to the front-runner from a prominent tracking position.

runners_data.name: Summergrounds
runners_data.note: A 70-day absence and a move to Good ground after all five recent runs came on Soft are the main flags here; naturally a prominent racer, he finds himself behind more established pace horses in this field and may not secure a forward pitch, blunting the aggressive style that underpins his best form.

races.paceDynamic: Supreme Yeats is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with only four runners on Good ground over 2m3½f, he is almost certain to dictate from the front without any genuine pressure from the field. Crystal Glance is a prominent-going type who will likely track Supreme Yeats in second, while Summergrounds — a natural front-runner redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — is unlikely to secure that berth and will be shuffled further back than ideal. Il Va De Soi, a genuine hold-up horse, will settle at the rear and rely on a well-judged ride from Theo Gillard to arrive late. The absence of a pace duel, coupled with Good ground and a small field, strongly favours horses capable of travelling prominently and switching off, with stamina and jump accuracy coming to the fore in the final half-mile — the profile of a prominent racer with sound jumping rather than a closer waiting on others to fold.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Supreme Yeats Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Supreme Yeats bowls along at a true but sustainable gallop and jumps accurately throughout, pinching a decisive advantage by the home turn.
scenarios.body: If Supreme Yeats bowls along at a true but sustainable gallop and jumps accurately throughout, pinching a decisive advantage by the home turn.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Crystal Glance Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Supreme Yeats jumps untidily or fades inside the final two hurdles, allowing Crystal Glance to collar him off a prominent pitch.
scenarios.body: If Supreme Yeats jumps untidily or fades inside the final two hurdles, allowing Crystal Glance to collar him off a prominent pitch.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Il Va De Soi Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong enough to string the field out and Il Va De Soi produces a sustained run from the rear on ground that fully suits.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is strong enough to string the field out and Il Va De Soi produces a sustained run from the rear on ground that fully suits.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Summergrounds Bounces Back
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls and Summergrounds is allowed to find a prominent position despite the redistribution and his 70-day absence.
scenarios.body: If the field crawls and Summergrounds is allowed to find a prominent position despite the redistribution and his 70-day absence.

watchPoints.text: Supreme Yeats — watch his jumping closely throughout; if he makes a significant error at any of the hurdles in the back straight it could instantly change the dynamic of this otherwise processional race shape.

Summergrounds — his 70-day absence combined with a switch to Good ground (all recent form on Soft) means fitness and going suitability are genuine questions; a flat or laboured jump early would confirm he is not at his best.

Il Va De Soi — monitor in-running position; if the tempo is modest and he is more than five lengths off the pace after halfway, the hold-up tactics may be impossible to make pay in a four-runner field.

Crystal Glance — watch whether Jack Tudor pushes him to go with Supreme Yeats immediately or settles just behind; the former risks a pace battle that suits the front-runner, the latter is the smarter tactical play given Good ground and a small field.

races.name: Rachel Jones Memorial Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Into Battle
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton's stable companion to Evening Tess, this five-year-old has shown a genuine hold-up style with two wins at around this trip on good ground (sim-going 2W5P) and arrives 42 days fresh — the conditions and profile suit, and Robert Dunne has the tactical nous to hunt down a lone leader.|

runners_data.name: Centurion's Sister
runners_data.note: Nicky Richards' six-year-old is the race's sole pace-setter and will get a completely uncontested lead, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is a reminder that she is racing slightly outside her most effective role — her sim-going record (0W3P) suggests she converts lead into place money rather than wins, so the key question is how much she has left from the last.|

runners_data.name: Evening Tess
runners_data.note: Dan and Harry Skelton have been firing at a 13/23 14-day strike rate and this four-year-old arrives just 16 days after a win, carrying good recent form (last five: 1-2-2) on going she clearly handles; a natural hold-up type with strong finishing form at the trip, she is ideally placed to pounce if the front-runner weakens.|

runners_data.name: American Empire
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's six-year-old is at heart a hold-up horse but has been redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear is oversubscribed — running from a position not truly his own (STYLE_FIT 0.90) tempers confidence; headgear noted, 52 days off, and a sim-going record of just 1W4P on similar conditions mean this is a situational runner at best.|

runners_data.name: Prettylady
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor partners this lightly-weighted four-year-old who has won back-to-back on good ground (sim-going 2W2P), but her true instinct is to come from the back and the redistribution to midfield is not where she naturally settles — the Greenall/Guerriero yard is 0/3 in the 14-day window, and a tricky trip around Bangor adds further uncertainty to an already compromised tactical position.|

races.paceDynamic: Centurion's Sister is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rivals for the lead in a five-runner field, Danny McMenamin can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 2m½f trip on good ground. That uncontested lead creates a classic set-pace scenario where Centurion's Sister will travel comfortably throughout, facing no early pressure and dictating the fractions through the Bangor bends. The three true hold-up horses — Into Battle, American Empire, and Prettylady — will track from behind, but because the map holds more hold-up types than the rear can accommodate, American Empire and Prettylady have been pushed into midfield positions that are not truly their natural habitat, meaning their style-fit is compromised. This race shape — a single, uncontested front-runner controlling a modest tempo — squarely favours hold-up horses with the class and finishing kick to reel in the leader late, with Evening Tess and Into Battle best placed to exploit that profile on going they handle well.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Centurion's Sister bowls along uncontested and the strong-finishing hold-up types get a clear run from the second-last.
scenarios.body: If Centurion's Sister bowls along uncontested and the strong-finishing hold-up types get a clear run from the second-last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is so modest that Centurion's Sister retains enough energy to repel all challengers from the last hurdle home.
scenarios.body: If the tempo is so modest that Centurion's Sister retains enough energy to repel all challengers from the last hurdle home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If American Empire or Prettylady settle better than expected in their redistributed midfield slots and produce a sustained run from three out.
scenarios.body: If American Empire or Prettylady settle better than expected in their redistributed midfield slots and produce a sustained run from three out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Jumping Errors
scenarios.trigger: If one or more runners makes significant jumping errors that reshuffle the field and open up ground for a horse tracking wide or travelling strongly.
scenarios.body: If one or more runners makes significant jumping errors that reshuffle the field and open up ground for a horse tracking wide or travelling strongly.

watchPoints.text: Centurion's Sister settles uncontested at the front — watch whether Danny McMenamin tries to steal the race by injecting pace from three out, which could catch the hold-up horses flat-footed.

American Empire and Prettylady are being asked to race in midfield rather than their natural rear positions — watch for unsettled behaviour early or a failure to travel, which would effectively remove them from contention before the race is half-run.

Into Battle has had 42 days off and could need the run — watch how sharply Robert Dunne asks him to quicken from the second-last, as a slightly ring-rusty performance could see him fail to close the gap in time.

Evening Tess arrives on the back of a recent win and the Skelton yard is in strong form (T14: 13/23) — watch her jumping throughout, as a clean round from a horse of her profile in this small field could make the result straightforward if the tempo is right.

With only five runners on good ground at Bangor, the field is likely to bunch in the back straight — watch for traffic issues developing approaching the home turn, particularly around the redistributed midfield runners who may not get the cleanest of passages.

races.name: Tom Jones Live At Chester Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Collingham
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer with strong good-ground hurdle form — his historical sim-going record (11 runs, 4 wins or places on Good) stands out in this field, and over a 2m7f trip that stretches stamina the 213-day absence is the one flag to watch alongside a conditional jockey booking.

runners_data.name: Roxboro River
runners_data.note: Has been busy (ran 14 days ago) but his form string of 4-7-7-10-11 on consistently good ground makes for grim reading; all 15 career runs on similar going have yielded just one win or place, and trainer Hanlon's 14-day record of 0/24 adds further caution.

runners_data.name: Rock Hurley
runners_data.note: McCain's runner is a genuine closer at heart — his best recent effort was a third on Good over 2m — but he's been squeezed forward on the map simply because the field has too many hold-up types; his three-run good-ground record (0 wins, 1 place) is thin, and the tongue-tie is noted.

runners_data.name: Innisfree Lass
runners_data.note: The only confirmed pace-setter in the race, making her the pivotal horse tactically; her entire recent form has come on soft ground and her solitary good-ground run in the last 15 races (0 wins, 0 places) is a genuine concern, though a solo lead at 2m7f on an easy track is a significant compensating factor.

runners_data.name: Golden Glance
runners_data.note: Won over 2m on Good most recently and is in form, but his natural preference is to race further back than the map shows — he's a true hold-up horse pushed into midfield here by the crowd of closers, which means the winning position he wants may simply not be available without an entirely different race shape.

runners_data.name: Jay Bee Whiskey
runners_data.note: Returns from a very long absence (last run 584 days ago with a pulled-up run sandwiched in) and has only one run on comparable going in recorded history; his tongue-tie and the sheer extent of the layoff make him extremely difficult to assess, and his natural hold-up style is compromised by redistribution.

runners_data.name: Athena's Dream
runners_data.note: The youngest runner at four and the only one with an unknown style rating, giving her tactical flexibility; she placed over 2m4f on Good last time out which is encouraging form and distance-wise, and the claim of Megan Bevan (8lb allowance) brings the weight down meaningfully at 145lbs, though she is unproven at 2m7f.

runners_data.name: The Kings Soldier
runners_data.note: In-form by recent standards with two third-place finishes in his last four over 2m4f on Good, but his true instinct is to race from the rear — shown at the back of the map only because the hold-up section is oversubscribed — and a 5-year-old on a low OR of 74 with a conditional jockey faces a stiff task off this trip.

races.paceDynamic: Innisfree Lass is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 2m7f conditional jockeys' handicap hurdle and, with no rival likely to press her hard, she should control a steady, sustainable gallop from the front over this stamina-testing trip on good ground at Bangor. The field is loaded with hold-up types — Rock Hurley, Golden Glance, Jay Bee Whiskey, and The Kings Soldier are all genuine closers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there is no room to show them all at the rear — meaning the true nature of this race is a lone leader followed by a pack of horses racing closer than they would prefer. With Innisfree Lass setting a controlled tempo and no credible prominent rival to push her wide or quicken the pace, the race will likely be run at a measured gallop that suits a front-runner who stays well, before the chasing pack mounts a challenge from two out. This race shape strongly favours Innisfree Lass if she can convert her natural lead, but a sustained-run, stamina-based finish from two out could also play into the hands of any closer who travels fluently in the pack — with the critical caveat that the redistributed hold-up horses will be racing out of their most comfortable position, which undermines their chance in a shape that depends on a true late run from off the pace.

scenarios.title: Innisfree Lass Controls

scenarios.body: If Innisfree Lass bowls along at a comfortable clip and no rival forces a test of pace early.

scenarios.title: Closers Wear Her Down
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just slow enough to keep the whole field within striking range turning in, allowing the chasing pack to close collectively.
scenarios.body: If the pace is just slow enough to keep the whole field within striking range turning in, allowing the chasing pack to close collectively.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Staying Test Ruthless
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop quickens early in the back straight, stringing the field out and turning the race into a pure stamina examination.
scenarios.body: If the gallop quickens early in the back straight, stringing the field out and turning the race into a pure stamina examination.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Midfield Bunching
scenarios.trigger: If several of the redistributed hold-up horses push forward early, creating an uncharacteristically pressured and messy pace scenario.
scenarios.body: If several of the redistributed hold-up horses push forward early, creating an uncharacteristically pressured and messy pace scenario.

watchPoints.text: Innisfree Lass has run just once on good ground in her last 15 starts for zero wins or places — if she struggles to handle the faster surface her solo-lead advantage could evaporate entirely, dramatically opening the race.

With five genuinely redistibuted hold-up types (Rock Hurley, Golden Glance, Jay Bee Whiskey, The Kings Soldier, plus Collingham and Roxboro River), watch the early stages closely — if several push forward against their nature, the first-circuit gallop could become far more pressured than the pace map suggests.

Jay Bee Whiskey's 584-day absence and mid-race pulled-up run make him a significant safety consideration in a conditional jockeys' hurdle — watch for erratic jumping or early signs of distress that could compromise horses tracking him.

Athena's Dream's 8lb claim for Megan Bevan is the largest weight relief in the race and brings her into a competitive weight bracket at 145lbs — if she travels fluently in midfield she could emerge as a value factor in the straight even without a strong going or trip profile.
